binding_record_note: Two native const allocator-handle Clear overloads join to real compiler-emitted borrowed Rust methods. Records remain partial and grant zero global API or original-test mapping credit.
changes: Added clear_with_borrowed_allocator to both ordered containers without key/value Debug, Clone or policy HashPolicy bounds. Borrowing retains the replacement handle until the native post-destruction assignment phase.

Both borrowed and consuming routes share clear_allocator_nodes. The borrowed route clones a different replacement only after Clear returns; the consuming convenience retains its prior owned-argument behavior.

Native same allocator handles retain buckets; different or null handles release buckets. Null selects the common allocator only after successful destruction, including when the old allocator was already common.
The sole BaseMapStorage owns the selected allocator. Key/value Drop observations use actual allocator counts and active raw allocations without a synthetic count adjustment.

Forty-eight native normal cases cover two families, custom/common old allocators, same/other/null/current selections and empty/filled/retained-empty graphs. Four explicit temporary-owned native profiles certify existing consuming convenience behavior.

Twelve native noexcept destructor failures run in isolated child processes with a terminate handler recording the valid failure prefix and exit 73. Rust compares those callback prefixes, then separately asserts its documented recovery: all nodes freed, old allocator retained, bucket-release choice honored and subsequent reuse working.

Common allocator absolute baseline counts are captured in raw native stderr; comparisons use observed changes from the pre-construction baseline because loaded native globals own additional common handles.
limitations: This bounded borrowed-argument method slice does not establish class-wide or global API/test parity.

Native throwing payload destructors terminate; Rust catches individual payload panics, completes node cleanup and resumes the first panic. Only the callback prefix before the first throw is compared across this boundary; final native termination state is archived, not claimed equal to Rust recovery.

Native Clear(map.Allocator()) aliases its member handle. Safe Rust cannot simultaneously borrow that member and mutably borrow the map; the equivalent current-allocator operation remains clear(false), covered by the self cases.

Normal Clear does not allocate replacement nodes. Allocator assignment uses the existing Arc-based handle adaptation; arbitrary foreign custom allocator destruction callbacks and allocation-failure termination are not certified.
Native POSIX fork/wait isolation is a Linux oracle harness feature, not a Rust kernel dependency.
Safe detached cursor owner validation, registry overhead, raw bucket mutation contracts and set node unit views remain separately tracked representation adaptations.
Scoped native/compiler/Miri evidence does not replace whole-workspace validation or the global API completeness proof.
compiler_warning_note: Nightly rustdoc warnings outside this borrowed Clear scope are retained in raw output; scoped Clippy is run with warnings denied.
